newsitem.title: UK: Euro straight-run sell numbers defy crude's effect.
newsitem.headline: Euro straight-run sell numbers defy crude's effect.

text.p: European straight-run sellers were clinging on to their offer levels on Tuesday in the face of crude's hefty fall, traders said.
Low sulphur straight-run offers were at $109-$110 fob a tonne in the morning with buyers reluctant to come above $106-$107.
With two prominent buyers and two cargoes seen mid-month the market looked balanced until crude dropped after the NYMEX opened.
But sellers dug in their heals and lowered their offer levels by just $1, in the hope refinery appetite for straight-run persisted.
"I'm still hearing $106-$107 on the bid side, despite the fall in crude," said one seller. "It's more a supply issue than a crude issue. We still see competition on the demand side."
Russian straight-runs were still sporadic in the north, with the two good quality M-100 cargoes from Tallinn believed to have earned good premiums.
One was heard to have sold yesterday for two means plus $4.50. The second went on Tuesday for two means plus $5.50, one trader said.
